Configure an OpenFOAM case for a 2D compressible supersonic jet simulation using rhoCentralFoam.
The physical model is air as a perfect gas using hePsiThermo with equationOfState perfectGas and transport model sutherland.
The nozzle inlet boundary has fixedValue conditions: U = (686 0 0) m/s, p = 101325 Pa, T = 300 K, corresponding to Mach 2.0 at sea-level stagnation conditions.
The far-field and outlet boundaries use waveTransmissive for p and T, and zeroGradient for U.
All solid walls (nozzle body and any symmetry or ground planes) use noSlip for U, zeroGradient for p and T.
The mesh is 2D: a single-cell-thick extrusion in the z-direction with frontAndBack patches set to type empty.
Choose a domain that is clearly larger than the inlet opening in both x and y; for example, an inlet nozzle height of 0.02 m with a domain of approximately 0.4 m x 0.2 m is a reasonable starting point.
Target a structured or blockMesh-style grid on the order of 400 cells in x and 200 cells in y to resolve the jet shear layer and shock structures near the inlet while keeping cell count manageable for initial validation.
Set simulationType to laminar in constant/turbulenceProperties.
In system/controlDict set application to rhoCentralFoam, choose an appropriate end time (for example 0.01 s) and write interval, and set the Courant number to a value safe for explicit Godunov schemes (approximately 0.4 or lower).
Ensure grad(p) and div schemes are consistent with rhoCentralFoam expectations (bounded Gauss linear for gradient, vanLeer or NVD for divergence of U).
Provide all standard OpenFOAM case directories: 0, constant, system, with field files for U, p, T, e, and phi initialized consistently with the inlet values and freestream conditions.
